# Vitals knowledge rules, shipped with Vitals. One rule per line:
#   kind | match | extra | severity | message
# kind:
#   dll      match = DLL file name in Data\F4SE\Plugins. extra = "refused" (only when it is not running) or "-".
#   needs    match = text found inside a DLL. extra = file it needs, relative to the game folder.
#   conflict match and extra = two files relative to the game folder ({ENB} = an ENB is installed). Both present -> issue.
#   Special names: {ENB}, {ADDRESS_LIBRARY} (the Address Library file for the running game version).
#   oldfile  match = loose file relative to the game folder. extra = date YYYY-MM-DD. Older than that -> issue.
#   file     match = file relative to the game folder. Present -> issue.
#   dllbuild match = DLL file name in Data\F4SE\Plugins. extra = the plugin version that DLL reports about itself (as in the
#            report, for example 0.0.4.13; a shorter version such as 0.0.4 matches every sub-build). The DLL must be running.
#            Only the DLL's own version counts, never a file date. Vitals before 0.4.2 skips this kind.
#   patchedby match = part of a game function's name (any case). extra = the DLL that normally patches it. Used only to say, in
#            the address check, "normally patched by X, which is running"; severity is not used (write info). Never a finding.
#   Any kind can name the game versions it applies to: oldfile@NG,AE (OG = 1.10.163, NG = 1.10.980/984, AE = 1.11.x).
#   Without it the rule applies to every version. Vitals before 0.4.0 skips rules with a version list.
# A header line "# Generated: YYYY-MM-DD" gives a file a date. When two files hold the same rule, the file read first wins:
# files without a date first (in name order), then dated files, newest first. The report header lists the files used.
# severity: problem (may crash the game; always shown in the start-up box) | warning | info.
# A 'dll ... refused' rule's message becomes the advice for that DLL in the report (its severity is used if higher).
# Every rule here comes from a finding we confirmed in game (Defib census notes, dates given). Add your own rules
# in another .txt file in this folder; Vitals reads all of them. Updating Vitals replaces this file and defib-census.txt only.

# The rules found by the Defib census are in defib-census.txt next to this file (generated from the census
# repository; it is replaced by updates too). This file keeps the format notes above and any rule that does not
# come from the census. If the same rule is in two files, Vitals uses it once.

# Independent Weapon Facing (Nexus 108957): its page says it was made for Old-Gen 1.10.163 only; the 7.4 DLL has
# F4SEPlugin_Query but no F4SEPlugin_Version, and F4SE 0.7.9 skips it on AE 1.11.240 (confirmed 2026-11-15).
dll@NG,AE | IndependentWeaponFacing.dll | refused | warning | Independent Weapon Facing's page says it was made for Old-Gen 1.10.163 only, so it does nothing on Next-Gen or Anniversary.

# --- Which DLL normally patches a game function (used only to word the address check; see "patchedby" above) ---
# From each mod's own description of what it patches, not from a launch with the DLL removed: unconfirmed. The report only
# names a DLL that is running, and says "normally patched by".
patchedby | MemoryManager:: | Addictol.dll | info | Addictol replaces the game's memory manager and scrap heap.
patchedby | ScrapHeap:: | Addictol.dll | info | Addictol replaces the game's memory manager and scrap heap.
patchedby | CheckModsLoaded | AchievementsEnablerAE.dll | info | Achievements Enabler patches the check that turns achievements off when mods are loaded.
patchedby | GetEncounterZone | encounter_zone_recalculation.dll | info | The encounter zone recalculation fix patches this function.
